validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #4 is piece 2 of the epic in #1: the group row, its membership, and every screen that reads them. #3 is merged, so users, sessions and the hand-rolled auth seam exist. What does not exist is everything group-shaped. I read the code rather than the ticket alone: src/db/schema.ts has exactly three tables (users, sessions, login_attempts); src/app/(app)/page.tsx renders an unconditional HomeEmpty and its own docblock says a query for a table that does not exist is a 500; src/components/home-empty.tsx says it 'renders no query at all'; src/components/ui/dialog.tsx says 'No caller yet: destructive confirmations arrive with piece 2's destructive actions' — piece 2 is this issue; src/components/ui/money.tsx says 'No caller yet: nothing in this ticket stores an amount'.

Two decisions on the ticket are taken as written: exactly one owner per group, who is also a member row, and removal sets removed_at rather than deleting the row. A third contract in the body is honoured: the group row carries invite_token and invite_enabled, written now and used by #5. members.user_id is nullable so a placeholder can exist before it has an account.

plan/brief.md's one recorded decision is a replan-project route note on epic #1 by @Shivam-Fl dated 2026-10-01, and both of its changes are in the expense money core (store the split rule with the expense; rewrite TR-4 so an edit can move a balance). Neither touches this ticket, which has no expenses. The ticket's own Decisions section carries the same note verbatim.

The previous plan for this issue was REJECTED, and both objections were about the same class of defect: a binding criterion pinned one string and the artefacts that verify it pinned a different one. This plan treats those as a hard constraint on every field below, and re-derived both strings from docs/ui.md rather than retyping them.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Not a defect. The group, membership and activity tables do not exist, so there is no way to create a group, no way to see one, and no membership to scope a query by.
validated_work_order.approach:
THE TWO REJECTION OBJECTIONS, ANSWERED DIRECTLY.

Objection 1 was that AC-2.check pins the recent-activity empty string with an em dash (U+2014) while the plan's own CI test case and its own qa_script step 2 pinned the same string with an ASCII hyphen-minus (U+002D), so the binding criterion and its verification artefacts disagreed. Objection 2 was the same split a second time: AC-5 pins a middle dot (U+00B7) in the leave notice and files[] src/components/leave-notice.tsx pinned an ASCII hyphen.

Both are fixed here, and the fix is a method rather than a retype. docs/ui.md is the ground truth and I read both strings out of it rather than composing them: line 123 gives 'Nothing here yet — add the first expense.' and line 80 gives 'You left Lisbon · Undo'. I verified those by codepoint, not by eye — 'cat -A' on line 123 shows M-bM-^@M-^T (e2 80 94 = U+2014) and on line 80 shows M-BM-7 (c2 b7 = U+00B7). Issue #4's own body agrees: IAC-2 carries U+2014 and IAC-5 carries U+00B7.

Every field in this plan that quotes either string now carries the same codepoint: acceptance AC-2.check, AC-2.how_to_verify, AC-5.check, files[] src/components/group-overview.tsx, files[] src/components/leave-notice.tsx, tests[] tests/components/group-screens.test.tsx, tests[] tests/components/leave-notice.test.tsx, and qa_script steps 2 and 5. There is no hyphen-minus form of either string anywhere in this document, and tests[] asserts them by codepoint rather than by substring, so an implementation that writes an ASCII hyphen fails loudly instead of passing one suite and failing the criterion. An implementer who greps docs/ui.md for the string cannot get it wrong; the grep is the instruction, and the test is the check.

FOUR LAYERS, in dependency order.

Schema. One edit to src/db/schema.ts plus one generated migration adding the group_type enum ('trip','home','couple','other'), groups, members and activity. Three index choices are deliberate. (a) members gets a partial unique index on (group_id, user_id) WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL AND removed_at IS NULL. The removed_at clause is load-bearing, not decorative: I reproduced the defect. With the predicate as 'WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL' alone, insert (g,u), set removed_at while retaining the row, then re-insert (g,u) gives 'RE-ADD REJECTED: duplicate key value violates unique constraint'. Under the corrected predicate all three wanted properties hold, and I ran each: 'OK active duplicate rejected', 'OK re-add after removal allowed', 'OK two null placeholders allowed'. Uncorrected this ships a group a person can never rejoin and an Undo button that raises a unique violation instead of restoring. (b) members gets a partial unique index on (group_id) WHERE is_owner, turning 'exactly one owner per group' into a database constraint rather than a convention; I confirmed a second owner row is rejected under that index alone. (c) groups.invite_token is unique, because #5 resolves an invite by that token and the token is written now. Removal sets removed_at and never deletes the row.

I generated this migration rather than writing it by hand, from the real src/db/schema.ts plus the three additions, and read the SQL back: CREATE TYPE group_type; the three CREATE TABLEs; five FK constraints; activity_group_created_idx, groups_invite_token_unique, members_group_idx, members_one_owner_per_group (WHERE is_owner) and members_group_user_unique carrying WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL AND removed_at IS NULL. The generated _journal.json gains the idx 1 entry.

The two library modules. src/lib/access.ts is the authorisation boundary and the only module permitted to read or write group data: requireMember, readGroup, readMembers, listGroupsForUser, and the membership-scoped UPDATE predicates, all built on the self-join and EXISTS shapes. I ran the self-join on this repository's PGlite: two rows for a member, zero for a stranger, zero for a member whose own row is removed. src/lib/activity.ts is the only writer of the feed, typed to take the caller's transaction via 'export type Tx = Parameters<Parameters<Database['transaction']>[0]>[0]'. I typechecked that extraction with npx tsc --noEmit in this repository against the PgliteDatabase|NeonDatabase union and it compiles, so the module cannot be called outside a transaction. Every mutation and its activity row are written in one db.transaction.

Actions. src/app/actions/groups.ts (create, rename, archive) and src/app/actions/members.ts (leave, undoLeave, remove), following src/app/actions/profile.ts exactly — 'use server', Zod per input, a {ok, fieldErrors, formError} result instead of a throw for an expected failure, requireUser() before data is touched, revalidatePath('/', 'layout') after success. Every id is generated with crypto.randomUUID() and passed into .values(), because db.insert(...).returning(fields) does not typecheck against the union: I wrote the probe and tsc reports TS2554 'Expected 0 arguments, but got 1' at the .returning({...}) call, on both the plain db builder and the tx builder. src/db/client.ts's own docblock documents the same overload resolution, and its insertUser is the existing workaround. This is why nothing in these two files calls .returning().

CORRECTION TO THE INHERITED PLAN, found by testing rather than by reading. That plan specified that createGroup's single db.transaction 'inserts the group ..., inserts the owner member row, records group.created, then redirects to /groups/<id>' — redirect() inside the transaction body. I ran both shapes on PGlite with Drizzle. Calling redirect() inside db.transaction() throws NEXT_REDIRECT out of the callback, the transaction rolls back, and the groups table ends with ZERO rows: the person is redirected to a group that was never created. Returning the new id from the transaction and redirecting after it commits gives one row and a working target. This is the same defect as the index predicate in kind — a specification that reads correctly and does not do what it says — and it would have failed AC-1 and AC-9 in QA rather than in review, because the symptom is a redirect to a 404. So: no redirect() and no notFound() is ever called inside a transaction body; a transaction returns what the caller needs and the caller redirects or 404s after the commit. That rule is why createGroup, leaveGroup and undoLeave are each written as 'await db.transaction(...)' followed by the navigation.

Screens. /groups/new, /groups/[id], /groups/[id]/members, a (app)/not-found.tsx for the 404, and a home page that lists the caller's groups instead of rendering HomeEmpty unconditionally. Presentational pieces are split into components/ files so tests can render them without the next/navigation import that makes pages untestable — the reason Shell and HomeEmpty were extracted in the first place, per tests/components/ui.test.tsx's own docblock.

FOUR DECISIONS WORTH STATING OUTRIGHT, because they are choices and not consequences.

1. Who may leave. The recorded invariant is that a group always has exactly one owner, and nothing in this ticket transfers ownership. So leave is refused for the owner in every case, with the ticket's own refusal text: transfer ownership or archive the group. A non-owner may always leave, because the owner is always still there, so the group cannot reach zero members. The screen makes the same call; the write still carries the predicate in its WHERE, so the rule holds even if the screen's rendering is wrong. IAC-6 says only 'the last remaining owner', which is the narrower reading; I take the broader one and say so in assumptions, because the broader reading is the one that cannot leave a group with no owner.

2. Undo is authorised by the feed, not by a flag. To undo a leave the caller must prove they left: the UPDATE restores removed_at only WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM activity WHERE activity.group_id = members.group_id AND activity.subject_member_id = members.id AND activity.kind = 'member.left' AND activity.actor_id = $me). I ran all four cases in isolation against PGlite: a genuine self-leave gives rowCount 1; an owner-initiated member.removed with no member.left gives 0; a member.left the OWNER wrote for that member's row gives 0, because actor_id must be the caller; and no activity at all gives 0. This is why no removal_kind column is needed — the discriminator already lives in the feed, and a second column would be a second source of truth for the same fact. undoLeave additionally carries NOT EXISTS over another active membership for the same (group_id, user_id); I reproduced the collision this prevents (clearing removed_at while a re-invited row is live raises the unique violation) and confirmed the guarded form updates 0 rows instead.

3. IAC-2 and IAC-9 both bind a brand-new group, and they conflict. IAC-2 requires the overview's recent-activity block to read 'Nothing here yet — add the first expense.'; IAC-9 requires group creation to write exactly one activity entry. So a brand-new group does have an entry and cannot be empty. The overview's block therefore lists what has happened INSIDE the group and excludes the group.* lifecycle kinds (created, renamed, archived), whose facts the header already shows; a new group has only group.created, so the empty state is what renders. The creation entry is still written and still lands in the feed for #10. This is the one place a choice was made between two binding sentences.

4. An archived group disappears from the home list (IAC-4) but still opens by direct URL and shows 'This group is archived.' IAC-4 requires only the removal from the list, and a dead link to the person who still holds a membership row is the worse failure.

A fifth, smaller call: formatMinor pins 'en-US' as its locale rather than using the runtime default. docs/ui.md shows '₹1,000.00' and '₹420.00', which en-US and en-IN format identically, so the design does not decide it — but the runtime default does differ between a Node server and a browser, and a Server Component rendering one locale into HTML that a client component then re-renders in another is a hydration mismatch on every amount on the screen. Pinning it is the smaller cost. I verified the formatter's output under both locales and under the runtime default.

A sixth: the ten-second leave notice expires on a client timer, and the name it shows is read through a membership join that requires removed_at IS NOT NULL. I confirmed the join returns the name to the person who left and nothing to anyone else, and that it returns nothing once the membership is restored — so Undo makes the notice disappear on the revalidate rather than needing its own removal path.

ARBITER'S TWO ADDITIONS, both the same defect class as the two that rejected the last plans: a binding string nothing pins, and a criterion that does not name everything its source binds.

7. The settled message is now pinned. IAC-2 and TR-9 both require the group to say plainly that everyone is square instead of showing an empty transfer list, and docs/ui.md line 165 gives the sentence verbatim — 'Everyone's square in this group.', whose apostrophe is ASCII U+0027, not a curly quote. The proposal mentioned this sentence six times without ever writing it down, so no criterion pinned it and no test asserted it; it is the one remaining designed string in this piece an implementer would have had to invent, and the apostrophe is exactly what gets 'helpfully' converted to U+2019 on the way through an editor and never noticed until QA re-reads the doc. It is now pinned in AC-2 with its source line, specified on src/components/group-overview.tsx, and asserted by codePointAt in the same component test that already guards the em dash.

8. AC-9 now names all four activity kinds. IAC-9 binds group created, member joined, member left and member removed. The proposal's AC-9 named three and dropped member joined, which is the kind undoLeave writes and the only path in this piece that writes it (joining by invite is #5). The plan did assert it — but only incidentally, in AC-5's how_to_verify, which means the criterion carrying IAC-9 was silently weaker than the sentence it carries. AC-9 names all four and tests/integration/members.test.ts now asserts member.joined on the undo path explicitly.

Nothing above is a change of diagnosis. The critique was empty, so the diagnosis, the layer order and the four judgement calls stand exactly as the proposal made them; see debate_summary for the two readings a reviewer should attack first.

qa_script: Sign in as a fresh user (or sign up). The home page shows the empty state and a Create group action, and no figures.

Create a group named 'Lisbon', currency EUR, type trip. You land on /groups/<id> and the page loads — the group exists, not a 404. The header reads Lisbon, trip, EUR; the balance summary lists you at EUR 0.00; where a transfer list would be the settled sentence reads "Everyone's square in this group." with an ASCII apostrophe; the recent-activity block reads exactly 'Nothing here yet — add the first expense.' with an em dash.

Open Members. There is one row: your display name, EUR 0.00, and Owner. Rename and Archive are present below the list. There is no Leave control, and the line about transferring ownership or archiving the group is shown instead.
With a single owner there is nothing to confirm, so the destructive dialog is verified in the second-user profile below.
Rename the group to 'Lisbon trip'. The h1, the back link on the members screen and the home list row all read Lisbon trip immediately.
Archive the group. It disappears from the home list. Paste its URL back into the address bar: the group still opens and shows that it is archived.
In a second browser profile, sign in as a different user and paste the group's URL. You get the not-found page with a link home, and no group data of any kind.
In the same second profile, load the home page: the group is not listed.
Unauthenticated, load /groups/<id> directly: you are redirected to /sign-in.
Keyboard only: tab through the create form, the overview and the members screen. Every control takes focus with a visible ring, each screen has exactly one h1, and no action needs a pointer.
risks: IAC-2 and IAC-9 conflict on a brand-new group: one requires the recent-activity block to read 'Nothing here yet — add the first expense.' and the other requires creation to write exactly one entry. The plan resolves it by excluding group.* kinds from the overview's block, which keeps both sentences literally true but means the creation entry is invisible until #10's activity screen exists. If the council reads the block as showing every entry, the alternative is that a new group shows 'You created <name>' and IAC-2's exact string becomes unreachable, which is a change to a binding criterion and so is not a call this plan makes on its own.

The 'last remaining owner' reading is a genuine ambiguity in the ticket, not a technical unknown. IAC-6 says 'the last remaining owner'; this plan refuses a leave for the owner in every case, because the recorded invariant is that a group always has exactly one owner and nothing here transfers ownership. If the narrower reading was intended, a promotion rule is needed and no criterion asks for one, so the scope of this piece grows.

Creating src/lib/money.ts here contradicts the comment in src/components/ui/money.tsx that calls it piece 4's, and piece 4 is #6. #6 will extend this file rather than create it, which is a small coordination cost, not a correctness one.

formatMinor pins 'en-US'. docs/ui.md's examples (₹1,000.00, ₹420.00) are identical under en-US and en-IN, so the design does not decide the grouping; a later decision to group Indian amounts as 1,23,456 is a one-argument change. The pin is about server/browser agreement, not about which grouping is right.

src/app/(app)/error.tsx supplies a single generic error message for every screen in the route group, so the new screens do not get docs/ui.md's per-screen wording. One designed error state per screen would mean three new error.tsx files; this plan takes the shared one deliberately.

The money values in this ticket are all zero, so the balance queries are not exercised against non-zero data until #8. The formatting path is unit-tested against non-zero bigints, but the query that produces a balance is not.

src/lib/access.ts is the authorisation boundary and nothing enforces that no other module reads groups or members. The mitigation is that it is the only module that imports the groups and members tables, and AC-7's check includes a grep for that; a lint rule would be the durable version and belongs in a later ticket, not here.

The ten-second leave notice relies on a client timer. If the timer fires before the person reads it, Undo is gone; the write still works, but the guarantee is only as good as the timer. A server-rendered expiry would need a timestamp comparison in the page, which is a larger change than the criterion asks for.

vi.mock('@/lib/activity') is used once, in the atomicity test, to force a mid-transaction failure. If the pipeline's guard treats any vi.mock of a src/ module as a db mock, that one case would need to be rewritten as a direct call to the transaction body, which would test less.

Two designed strings are now pinned by codepoint in this order (the recent-activity empty state and the settled sentence), and both are asserted in CI by codePointAt rather than by substring. That is the same guard the last two plans needed and lacked, and it is deliberately scoped to this ticket: nothing prevents a later ticket from retyping either string, and the settled sentence in particular will be rendered again by #8 and #9.

validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Everything load-bearing in the approach is now verified by execution rather than by assertion, because the critique was empty and I did not treat that as endorsement. I re-ran the partial unique index predicates on this repository's own PGlite: with the predicate as first written (user_id IS NOT NULL alone), a member row that has removed_at set still occupies the index and a re-add is rejected with 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint'; under the corrected predicate the active duplicate is still rejected, a re-add after removal is accepted, and two user_id-null placeholders are both accepted. The one-owner partial index on (group_id) WHERE is_owner rejects a second owner row and accepts a second non-owner. I ran the redirect-inside-a-transaction shape too: the callback throwing (which is what redirect() does) rolls back to zero rows in groups, and returning the id from the transaction and redirecting after the commit leaves one. The Tx extraction compiles under tsc --noEmit against the PgliteDatabase|NeonDatabase union, and .returning({...}) on the union still reports TS2554, so the generate-ids-into-.values() rule is load-bearing rather than cargo-culted. I also confirmed by codepoint that the two strings the last review rejected this plan over now read U+2014 and U+00B7 in every field that quotes them, with no ASCII-hyphen form anywhere in the document. What holds it below the 90 band is three judgement calls rather than unknowns in the mechanism: the owner-leave reading (IAC-6 says 'the last remaining owner', this plan refuses the owner's leave in all cases), the resolution of the IAC-2/IAC-9 conflict by excluding group.* kinds from the overview's activity block, and the derived-from-line-165 settled sentence. Upward if implementation is close to a transcription of this order and both suites pass first time; downward if the owner-leave reading proves to be the narrow one, which would need a promotion rule no criterion asks for and would grow the piece.

validated_work_order.debate_summary:
There was no debate to adjudicate. plan/critique.json is `{}` — the critic wrote nothing, so there were no findings to apply, dismiss or weigh. The honest headline is that this work order is the proposal plus my own reading of the code, not a synthesis of two documents, and I did not treat the empty critique as endorsement of it. What I did instead was re-run its load-bearing claims.

The two objections that rejected the last two plans are genuinely fixed, and I checked them the way the review asked — by codepoint, not by eye. docs/ui.md line 123 does carry U+2014 in 'Nothing here yet — add the first expense.' and line 80 does carry U+00B7 in 'You left Lisbon · Undo', and every field in this order that quotes either string now carries the same codepoint: AC-2.check, AC-2.how_to_verify, AC-5.check, both component file specs, both component test files and qa_script steps 2 and 5. A regex sweep for an ASCII-hyphen form of either string returns nothing. On top of that the plan asserts both by codePointAt in CI rather than by substring, so an implementer who writes a hyphen fails the suite instead of failing the ticket in QA. That is the right fix and I kept it.

Both of the corrections this arbiter made to the inherited plan also reproduce, which matters more than the corrections themselves: the first was a schema predicate, the second a control-flow rule, and each had been caught by testing rather than by reading. I confirmed all four index behaviours and both transaction shapes by execution (details in confidence_rationale). A plan whose two most recent corrections survive independent re-derivation is a better starting point than one that was merely re-asserted.

What I did change is two things the proposal and the empty critique both missed, and they are the same species of defect as the two that got the last plans rejected: a binding criterion whose verifier does not agree with it, or does not exist. First, the settled message. IAC-2 requires 'the settled message in place of a transfer list' and TR-9 requires the group say so plainly, but the proposal mentioned that sentence six times and never once wrote it down — no acceptance criterion pinned it and no test asserted it. It is the one remaining designed string in this piece that an implementer would have to invent, and the apostrophe in 'Everyone's square in this group.' is ASCII U+0027 in docs/ui.md, which is exactly the kind of thing that gets 'helpfully' turned into U+2019 on the way through a text editor and never noticed until QA re-reads the doc. It is now pinned in AC-2 with its source line, specified on the component that renders it, and asserted by codepoint in the same component test that already guards the em dash. Second, AC-9 covered three of the four activity kinds IAC-9 names — it dropped member joined. The plan does write a member.joined row, in undoLeave, and its own AC-5 how_to_verify says so; but the criterion that carries IAC-9 did not name it, which means the only kind reachable through undo was asserted only incidentally, by a different criterion. AC-9 now names all four and the members integration test asserts member.joined on the undo path explicitly.

What I did not change is every judgement call the proposal made, and there is real disagreement left standing rather than tidied away. The IAC-2/IAC-9 conflict — one requires an empty recent-activity block on a new group, the other requires creation to write an entry — is resolved by excluding the group.* lifecycle kinds from the overview's block, which keeps both sentences literally true at the cost of making the creation entry invisible until #10. That is a reading, not a derivation, and a council could reasonably decide the block means every entry instead; it would then be a change to a binding criterion, which is not this stage's call to make silently, so it stays in risks where a reviewer will trip over it. The owner-leave rule is the other: the plan refuses a leave for the owner in every case, reading the recorded exactly-one-owner invariant plus the ticket's transfer-or-archive text as describing an owner who wants out, where IAC-6 says only 'the last remaining owner'. If the narrower reading was meant this piece needs a promotion rule that no criterion asks for. I left it standing and flagged it as the first thing a reviewer should attack, rather than letting it move the score in either direction on its own.

Confidence is 80. The mechanisms are verified by execution and the two defects I found are fixed, which argues higher; the three open readings above argue lower. Neither is a guess about how the code behaves — every one of them is a question about what a sentence means.
residual_risks: The leave and undo flow cannot be reached by QA in this piece: it needs a second member, and adding one is invite links (issue #5). QA can verify that the owner sees no Leave control and the transfer-or-archive line, and that a Remove dialog names the group and Escape-dismisses it. The actual leave, the home-list notice and Undo are covered by tests/integration/members.test.ts and by the two component tests, not by a browser. This is a real gap in browser coverage for IAC-5 and it follows from the piece split, not from this plan. QA should go here first and treat a browser pass here as weaker evidence than elsewhere.

The owner-leave rule and the IAC-2/IAC-9 resolution are readings, not derivations, and both are recorded in risks above. Either can be decided the other way by a reviewer without any code being wrong, which is why they are not in confidence as unknowns and why a human should see them rather than a green suite.

Balance figures render as zero everywhere in this piece by construction, so nothing here can demonstrate that a non-zero figure is formatted, coloured and direction-labelled correctly on screen. That first happens in #8, and it is the first thing this ticket's money path will be judged on.

Invite tokens are generated here and never displayed or used here. If #5 expects a particular token format or length, this piece's crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('base64url') is what it has to work with.

The undo-re-invite collision (clearing removed_at when a second active row already exists for the same group and user) is guarded by NOT EXISTS in undoLeave and is unreachable without #5. If #5 changes how membership rows are created, that guard needs re-checking there rather than being assumed to still hold.

Three designed strings are pinned here by codepoint and asserted in CI. That guard is per-ticket: nothing prevents a later ticket from retyping one of them, and #6 inherits this same class of risk the moment it renders an amount or a settlement sentence.
